author.name: Bryan T
credits: Bryan T (bryantysinger): LOFI2's design, DSP56300 code, tables, declaration, render gate and hardware testing, contributed to octabam (pull requests 657, 704 and 843, MIT).
octabam: Sam Banks; SDK, schema and harness (MIT). LOFI2's stereo shifter uses the allpass coefficients of octabam's BodeShift and its ring carrier follows octabam's WarpFold.

presentation.label: RING / SHIFT / CRUSH
presentation.summary: One modulator, ring mod or a stereo frequency shifter, followed by sample-rate and bit reduction on stock LO-FI's curves and a high-shelf cut.
presentation.overview: LOFI2 is an insert on its own effect ID, so stock LO-FI stays in the chooser beside it. MODE picks the modulator: RING multiplies the track by a carrier, DOWN and UP shift every partial by FREQ Hz with a stereo Hilbert pair. MIX is the modulator's depth; SRR and BRR run after it on stock LO-FI's measured rates and curve and stay live at MIX 0, and LPF is a -12 dB high shelf last in the chain. Every continuous knob glides to its new value over about 1.5 ms. The defaults are a passthrough.
highlights: Ring modulator with an exponential six-octave FREQ, LOW/HIGH range and L/R carrier phase
Stereo frequency shifter, up or down, with feedback
SRR and BRR matched to stock LO-FI in a native render (rates within 0.02 dB of droop, steps within 0.01 bit)
Passthrough at defaults; every continuous knob glides, no zipper steps above -70 dBFS in the render gate
usage: On an audio track that plays a sample, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to LOFI2 and press YES. Nothing changes yet: the defaults are a passthrough.

Press FX2 for the main page. Turn MIX (encoder B) to 127 and FREQ (encoder A) to 64: the track is ring-modulated. Raise SRR or BRR (encoders D and E) for sample-rate and bit reduction, and lower LPF (encoder F) from 127 to darken the result.

For the frequency shifter, hold FUNC and press FX2 and turn MODE (encoder C) to UP or DOWN; on the main page the third knob is now FDBK. To bypass, set MIX, SRR and BRR to 0 and LPF to 127, or choose NONE in FX2 SETUP.

controls.name: FREQ
controls.doc: Modulator frequency, exponential over six octaves from RNGE's base. RING: 2-130 Hz (LOW) or 60-4,000 Hz (HIGH). SHIFT: 2-128 Hz (LOW) or 31.25-2,000 Hz (HIGH). FREQ 0 is the base frequency, not silence.

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Modulator depth: crossfades the ring or shift output against the dry signal. Not a global wet/dry: SRR, BRR and LPF still act at MIX 0.

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: One knob, renamed by MODE. In DOWN and UP it is FDBK, the shifter's feedback (a ladder at f, f+d, f+2d), capped at 0.40 (0.45 before 0.1.1, where the top of FDBK could sustain itself). In RING the panel shows GAIN: make-up on the ring product, 0 dB at 0, +6 dB at 64, +11.9 dB at 127.

controls.name: SRR
controls.doc: Sample-rate reduction at stock LO-FI's measured rates: no reduction through 7, 8,018 Hz at 64, 3,564 Hz at 127. 0 is off.

controls.name: BRR
controls.doc: Bit-depth reduction on stock LO-FI's curve, round-to-nearest: about 13.5 bits removed at 64 and 20.8 at 127. 0 is full depth.

controls.name: LPF
controls.doc: High-shelf cut, last in the chain: -12 dB above a corner swept from 100 Hz at 0 to 16 kHz at 126. 127 takes it out of circuit bit for bit; turn down to darken.

controls.name: RNGE
controls.doc: FREQ's range (RNGE on the panel): LOW is sub-audio (tremolo in RING, slow swirl in SHIFT), HIGH is the audio range.

controls.name: MODE
controls.doc: RING is the ring modulator; DOWN and UP are the frequency shifter moving every partial down or up. Ring and shift are exclusive. A change ducks the modulator for 5 ms each way so it does not click.

controls.name: AMPH
controls.doc: Ring carrier's L/R phase offset, bipolar: -90 to +88.6 degrees, 0 at the centre. + puts R ahead. RING only.

limitations: 0.1.1 (octabam 7795adf0, the feedback cap; one DSP data word differs from 0.1.0) ran once over USB on an MKII, 22 October 2026: one instance on FX2 on a RAM-booted development twin of the beta base, beside RINGMOD SC 0.2; the issue 825 setting died away and the tester reported the other functions passing, by ear. No reload, power cycle, second instance or FX1 with 0.1.1. Hardware evidence for 0.1.0 (octabam 8250be0c) is one functional report over USB on an MKII, 20 October 2026, about 15 minutes beside five other modules: every mode, the fixed SHIFT by ear, two instances on one core and a third refused (DSP FULL); the base's self-test failed on ColdFire CPU (98.8 %, cause not confirmed). Reloads, a power cycle, BRR and LPF individually ran only with the source before it (21f6de90: card image with five SHIFT instances, and USB package 7ee9277f), which differs from 0.1.1 in seventeen DSP data words (sixteen coefficients and the cap). Eight instances and scenes are untested on a unit. Bryan T's own MKII reports are for his octabam builds.

Large: 838 program words and a 516-word table on each DSP core, 1,354 contiguous words. With stock DSP code built in it needs two adjacent stock reverbs given up (PLATE REV + SPRING REV, or SPRING REV + DARK REV); one reverb is not enough.

SHIFT executes 430 instructions/sample at worst in dsp_host (static 416 cycles), about 1.4x SPRING REV's worst case and dearer than every stock effect; RING is 274. The author ran eight instances at once, four per core, in UP, DOWN and RING on his MKII in his own build (build 12, the 21f6de90 instructions), and eight in SHIFT DOWN with FX1 empty in build 16 (this source).

Over USB the Modwerk base loads LOFI2 on demand into FX1 or FX2. It declares 637 cycles a sample (timed on an MKII with package 7ee9277f of 21f6de90, whose instructions are the same; only data words differ), so two instances fit on one DSP core when its other slots are free and a third is refused (DSP FULL).

In DOWN and UP, once sound has passed through, the output settles at about -83 to -94 dBFS instead of silence and stays there (dsp_host render; the upstream module does the same). RING and the reduction stages return to silence.

Native octabam refuses LOFI2 together with Analog BD: it is not on Analog BD's reviewed DSP companion list. A scratch-only probe with the list widened placed both only with all three reverbs, LO-FI, DJ EQ and CHORUS given up and LOFI2's table moved to X memory; that layout is unreviewed and untested.

In a card build only the FX2 chooser was built and captured, and FX1 in a card image was not run on a unit. Over USB the base loads it into FX1 as well; FX1 ran on an MKII with 21f6de90's USB package (7ee9277f), not with 0.1.0's or 0.1.1's.

Effect ID 0x09, placement priority 19 and layout letter F are Modwerk's; they were checked free against the modules in this tree. A project saved with octabam's LOFI2 (ID 0x1f) selects TAPEHEAD's ID here.

Four LOFI2 in SHIFT on one DSP core with an effect on FX1 can lock the unit: on the author's MKII, four in SHIFT on T5-T8 with FILTER on FX1 of T5-T8 locked it, on upstream main as well (0.1.0 is affected too; https://github.com/sambanks/octabam/issues/850, open, no guard yet). Eight in SHIFT DOWN with FX1 empty ran. Over USB the base admits at most two per core (637 declared cycles); a card build has no such guard, and the count at which it starts with FX1 in use is not known yet.
No single-knob bypass: a passthrough is MIX 0, SRR 0, BRR 0 and LPF 127, the defaults.
A parameter lock holds until the track's next trig, as it does for every stock parameter on this OS.

storage.label: DSP program / table
storage.conditions: Native build report, both payloads: 838 program words and one 516-word P table, placed contiguously (1,354 words). 132 words of state in each instance's own r7 block ($00-$83). No allocator buffer, no Y memory. A 416-byte descriptor clone and 218 bytes of label formatters in ColdFire flash.

processing.label: DSP instruction peak
processing.conditions: benchmark_stock_dsp.py's method in dsp_host (one instance per core, 16-sample blocks, null stub subtracted), fixed, moving and trig-split cases; stock SPRING REV 314, LO-FI 290, DJ EQ 331 under the same cases. Static cycle_count.py: 416 cycles/sample on the SHIFT path. Executed instructions, not chip cycles.

impact.conditions: One active instance in SHIFT at its dearest settings with moving controls and trig splits; RING is about 64% of that.

cpu.rationale: No ColdFire code: a cloned FX2 descriptor and two label formatters; the stock parameter pages publish the knobs as for any effect.

dsp.rationale: 430 executed instructions/sample worst case in SHIFT against 314 for stock SPRING REV, 290 for stock LO-FI and 331 for DJ EQ (the dearest stock effect) under the same dsp_host cases; RING is 274. Two Hilbert allpass pairs and nine glides. The author's MKII ran eight instances at once, four per core, in UP, DOWN and RING on his octabam build of this source.

memory.rationale: 1,354 contiguous program-memory words on each DSP core (838 code, 516 table), more than any single stock reverb's span (SPRING REV 1,063, DARK REV 1,067), so a static build gives up two adjacent reverbs. 132 state words per instance in the existing r7 block; no buffer.

tests.summary: 0.1.1: ported unchanged in DSP from octabam 7795adf0, the author's pull request 843 for octabam issue 825: SHIFT's feedback cap 0.45 to 0.40, one DSP data word. A private native build passes all 73 checks of the author's render gate, including his three new ones: at FDBK 127, RNGE HIGH, DOWN FREQ 64 and 72 and UP FREQ 72, the tail after a burst settles at -69.2, -71.7 and -84.5 dBFS (0.1.0's source sustains about -4 dBFS there and fails exactly those three). Static count 416, the dsp_host benchmark and the stress run repeat 0.1.0's figures; the USB package differs from 0.1.0's in three bytes. On 22 October 2026 0.1.1's USB package a2ab2732 ran on the contributor's MKII (RAM-booted development twin 53ddaf60 of the beta base, one instance on FX2 beside RINGMOD SC 0.2): the issue 825 setting (DOWN, RNGE HIGH, FREQ 64, MIX 127, FDBK 127) died away, and the tester reported LOFI2's other functions passing; by ear, no reload or power cycle. The author reports the same on his MKII in his own octabam build. Everything below is 0.1.0's record (octabam 8250be0c): the author's optimised LOFI2 (pull request 704) with his SHIFT fix 153063d8 (Hilbert coefficients squared). A private native build on Modwerk's ID 0x09 passed all 70 checks of the author's render gate (the unwanted SHIFT sideband -45.7 to -56.2 dB at 1-15 kHz; SRR and BRR against stock LO-FI rendered from the tester's own OS 1.40C), plus dirty-state, init-register, menu, replaces, label and mode-name gates. Against the previous source (21f6de90) only 16 DSP coefficient data words differ. Static cost 416 cycles/sample; dsp_host benchmark 430 instructions/sample in SHIFT against LO-FI's 290 and SPRING REV's 314; a 32 s eight-instance stress run under memory guards had no hang and no clobber, and perf:audit passes with a justification. fx:audit is clean at the defaults and with the shelf in; in SHIFT a residue of -83 to -94 dBFS stays after the input stops, and at FDBK 124-127 with RNGE HIGH and FREQ about 60-76 the feedback sustains itself near full scale (dsp_host; the previous coefficients did the same at RNGE LOW, FREQ 127); on the MKII, UP at FREQ 64 HIGH with FDBK 127 kept a tone sounding after the input ended and FDBK 120 let it die away. Packages compile. On 20 October 2026 the USB package 4f794ebc ran on the contributor's MKII on flashed beta base 6650236a beside five other modules: install and Keep, every mode, FREQ, MIX, GAIN and SRR, the fixed SHIFT by ear, two instances on one core and a third refused; the base's self-test failed on CPU (98.8 % peak with six modules on an uncached base). The previous source's card-image and USB runs (13 and 15 October) are kept as history (evidence/hardware.md). Not tested on this source: BRR and LPF individually, the feedback case beyond UP at FREQ 64, reloads, a power cycle, eight instances and scenes.
gates: verify_lofi2.py: 73 dsp_host checks on payload A, including the SHIFT sidebands at 1, 3, 5, 10 and 15 kHz, the FDBK 127 tail settling (octabam issue 825) and SRR and BRR against stock LO-FI rendered from the tester's own image
verify_dirtystate, verify_initregs, verify_menu, verify_replaces, verify_labels, verify_modenames on the lofi2 test remix (static stock)
evidence/performance.json: perf:audit (static count, stock benchmark under matched cases, 32 s stress)
fx:audit at four settings; the SHIFT idle residue and the feedback scan measured separately
Isolated package compile with four-origin relocation proofs; a word-by-word diff of the DSP package against the previous source
evidence/hardware.md: a functional MKII report of this source's USB package, and the previous source's card-image and USB reports as history

conditions.parameterExtremes: tools/build/cycle_count.py prices the dearest path of the per-sample loop, SHIFT, at 416 cycles/sample; RING is cheaper. perf.py bench ran the manifest's dearest settings (every continuous knob at its costly end, LPF in band) in SHIFT UP, SHIFT DOWN and RING, the defaults, and the fixed and moving patterns: worst 430.06 executed instructions/sample.
conditions.parameterModulation: The moving pattern changes every active slot at every 16-sample block; the stress run adds three LFOs per track and a new value on every slot each sixteenth. LFOs, parameter locks, MIDI CC and scenes all arrive as the same knob words. A parameter lock was tried on a unit with 21f6de90 (the same instructions); scenes were not confirmed on a unit.
conditions.modeSwitching: The stress run redraws MODE and RNGE every sixteenth, so RING, DOWN and UP switch under load with the 5 ms duck; a trig split at every position 1-15 is in the benchmark (worst at 1). Re-selection runs init once. MODE was switched by hand on a unit with 0.1.0's source (8250be0c) and with 21f6de90; with 0.1.1's the tester reported the functions passing without per-mode detail; Part changes were not measured.
conditions.maxLoad: Four instances per core on FX2 of all eight tracks, behind DJ EQ (the dearest stock effect) on every FX1: 4 x 416 = 1,664 of 3,120 usable static cycles per core. dsp_host stress, 32 s, -guard -dirty: no hang, no clobber. Five SHIFT instances ran at once on a unit with 21f6de90; two on one core with 0.1.0's source (8250be0c); one with 0.1.1's. Hardware contradicts this load with FX1 occupied: the author's MKII locked with four SHIFT instances on T5-T8 and FILTER on FX1 of T5-T8, on upstream main as well (octabam issue 850, open; 4 x 416 + 4 x 192 = 2,432 static cycles, inside the model's budget). Streaming, USB and MIDI load are not in the model.
conditions.inputConditions: Stress stems: drums with full-scale clicks, a full-level chord, noise bursts and silence, a 20 Hz-20 kHz sweep, a full-scale square, impulses, DC steps and plucks. The sample loop's only signal-dependent branch is SRR's re-latch; the count takes the dearer arm.

regions.name: Program: 838 logical P words on each DSP core
Tables SRR_INC, BRR_E, BRR_M and LPF_C: 516 P words on each DSP core
Descriptor clone including its stride padding
RNGE and MODE formatter code and labels

memory.conditions: Native build report of the lofi2 test remix (stock DSP code built in), both payloads: table then code, contiguous. Each 132-word state block is the instance's existing r7 block, which init zeroes whole. No Y memory, no allocator buffer, heap, SDRAM or CPU RAM. Eight instances are FX2 of all eight tracks. Firmware storage packs DSP words in three bytes.

hardware.summary: Over USB on the contributor's Octatrack MKII, OS 1.40C, RAM-booted into a development twin of the beta base (identity 53ddaf60f435aedf…, MAIN.raw 712666cb…; main 4d4f731d plus two unmerged base fixes, the KEY step and key-bus admission, neither on LOFI2's path), installation driven over USB by a coordinating session, the tester listening. The USB package a2ab2732… (0.1.1) was accepted at generation 2 beside RINGMOD SC 0.2 and ran on FX2 of one track while it played. The issue 825 repro (SHIFT DOWN, RNGE HIGH, FREQ 64, MIX 127, FDBK 127: input played, then stopped): the tail died away, no feedback runaway. The tester checked LOFI2's other functions on the same build and reported that all pass, with no per-mode detail. LOFI2 was then removed over USB (accepted, generation 3). By ear; no level was measured (evidence/hardware.md).
limitations: One instance on one track; which track was not recorded. Two or more instances, FX1, the other DSP core and the full module set were not run with 0.1.1.
By ear only. The issue 825 setting was checked in DOWN at FREQ 64; FREQ 72 and UP were not reported separately, and the tail's level was not measured on the unit.
"All other functions pass" is the tester's summary; no per-mode or per-knob results were recorded.

A RAM-booted development twin with two unmerged base fixes, not a flashed release base; Part and project reload, a power cycle and persistence were not run with 0.1.1 (a RAM boot cannot show reboot persistence). Those ran only with source 21f6de90.
One MKII; the tester is the contributor of the port, not an independent reviewer.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial: ring, crush and shift a loop
steps: On an audio track that plays a sample, hold FUNC and press FX2, turn LEVEL to LOFI2 and press YES. Nothing changes yet: the defaults are a passthrough.

Press FX2 for the main page. Turn MIX (encoder B) to 127 and FREQ (encoder A) to 64: the track is ring-modulated. Raise SRR or BRR (encoders D and E) for sample-rate and bit reduction, and lower LPF (encoder F) from 127 to darken the result.

For the frequency shifter, hold FUNC and press FX2 and turn MODE (encoder C) to UP or DOWN; on the main page the third knob is now FDBK. To bypass, set MIX, SRR and BRR to 0 and LPF to 127, or choose NONE in FX2 SETUP.

access.location: Audio track FX2 SETUP: LOFI2 in the effect chooser.
steps: Select an audio track with its TRACK key.
Hold FUNC and press FX2 to open FX2 SETUP.
Turn LEVEL to LOFI2 and press YES to assign it; RNGE, MODE and AMPH appear on the right of the SETUP page.
Press FX2 for the main page: FREQ, MIX, GAIN (FDBK in DOWN/UP), SRR, BRR and LPF.
